frase_inicial: Michael: your financial health score is 26 today, and there is a clear path to improve it.

tarjetas.frente: January 2027 home purchase is the big fork in the road
tarjetas.reverso: If you go ahead without separating its cash, the down payment will eat the money you use to keep a cushion and to grow retirement savings. That makes short-term shocks more likely and reduces what your investments can do later.
tarjetas.detalle: Down payment needed January 2027: USD 113,300 (Michael). Planned mortgage monthly payment: USD 3,015.15 at 7% for 30 years.

tarjetas.frente: Your savings run out before the plan ends unless something changes
tarjetas.reverso: Retiring at 58 leaves a gap so savings would be exhausted by age 85, leaving planned spending unpaid in later years. That gap comes from current withdrawals and how near-term cash is used.
tarjetas.detalle: Savings and investments run out at age 85; unpaid planned spending at end: USD 32,439.

tarjetas.frente: Cash is thin today and the January goals drop it to zero
tarjetas.reverso: You have only about three months of expenses in accessible cash now. Setting aside the home down payment and the vacation would leave you with no cushion, so a small emergency would push you onto your credit card or force selling investments.
tarjetas.detalle: Accessible cash today: USD 30,000 (Michael). Cash target including goals: USD 163,330–172,636.

tarjetas.frente: Insurance leaves you exposed to a large liability or income loss
tarjetas.reverso: Your life cover and liability cover are well below recommended levels. If something serious happens, debts and lost income would fall on your assets and any dependent plans you care about.
tarjetas.detalle: Life cover: USD 180,000; recommended minimum: USD 900,000. Umbrella gap recommended: USD 1,000,000.

tarjetas.frente: High-interest credit card is the most expensive small debt
tarjetas.reverso: That card costs more than your other debts and is draining cash monthly. Paying it faster frees future cash but competes with building the emergency cushion and saving for the house or retirement.
tarjetas.detalle: Credit card balance: USD 3,500 at 20% APR; current monthly payment USD 200, projected payoff July 2028.

movimientos.title: Add umbrella cover
movimientos.action: Add $1M of umbrella to raise the liability shield

movimientos.title: Lower the withdrawal rate
movimientos.action: Cutting withdrawals to $10,300/year (6.0%) reaches the sustainable band

movimientos.title: Raise growth allocation toward glide
movimientos.action: Move the invested mix from 74% to 88% growth (glide 98%) for the next horizon-fit band — about $19,900 of the invested book

mapa.aviso: Illustrative simulator: it shows the direction of change, not a Sherpas projection.

siguiente_paso.razon: The plan flags no umbrella and recommends adding USD 1,000,000 to raise your liability shield; this directly reduces the risk that a claim would sweep your liquid assets and derail the home and retirement plans.
pasos: Call your auto or renter insurer and ask if they sell umbrella coverage and the annual premium for USD 1,000,000.
If they do not or the price is high, get two quotes from other insurers for the same USD 1,000,000 limit.
Choose the quote that fits your monthly budget and put the policy in place before closing the home purchase.
